commit.message:
fix(post): cap a feed that turns a rotary at the machine's stated rates

One prelude rule (post::rotary_cap: rotaryRate / rotaryFeedCap /
rotaryFeed / rotaryFeedWord) caps the F of every feed block that turns a
rotary so no rotary runs past its stated deg/min and no linear part past
the fastest stated feed, read the way each control reads F:

- fanuc.cps and doosan-dnm.cps under G43.4: F is the tool tip's speed,
  the rotaries carried along (F <= rate * tip / |d|; tip still: F <= rate).
- doosan-dnm.cps on a 4th axis without TCP and fanuc-lathe.cps C-axis
  live tooling: one composite length, degrees counted as mm.
  fanuc-lathe.cps now calls the shared rule instead of its own copy.
- Arcs that turn a rotary: the path rule over the chord in the arc's
  plane (never looser than any reading of an arc's F).

A capped F is floored to 0.1 mm/min. A feed that turns a rotary from an
angle the post never wrote is refused by name when that rotary states a
rate; each such refusal counts once per program. Unstated rates cap
nothing, so every golden posts byte-identical text. tormach.cps writes A
only on a G0 index and needs no cap.

fourth_axis_pose's tilted fixture now opens with a rapid that places the
rotary (its feeds would otherwise turn A from an unknown angle).

Fixes #885

fix(post): doosan-dnm writes the first A of each section, never assuming A0

Without TCP the post reset its modal A memory to 0 at program start, at
every tool change and at every section end, so an A0 operation after an
A30 one wrote no A word and cut at A30. The memory now starts and resets
to "unknown": the first tilted block of a program and of each section
writes its A (with the M11/M10 brake pair). With G43.4 the arm already
wrote the angles, but the brake was judged against the assumed A0; that
turn now unclamps too.

Pinned by doosan_dnm_a_state (new); rotary_feed_cap's Doosan
composite test now sees the opening A0 place the table instead of a
refusal. Stacked on #951 (#885).

Fixes #950

fix(post): a capped rotary feed is written in the program's unit (#951 review)

In an inch program the capped F went out as the mm/min number, so the
control read it as in/min and drove the rotary 25.4x past its stated
rate. rotaryFeedWord now takes the post's inch flag: mm/min floored to
0.1, or in/min floored to 0.001 - floored in both, so it never passes the
cap - with the "under 0.1 mm/min" refusal judged once, in mm, before
converting. The cap's linear length is judged between the points as
posted (the post's output step), since an inch word shortens a 0.1 mm
move to 0.0039 in and the control times the block over that.
fanuc.cps and doosan-dnm.cps cap a record carrying any of A, B or C,
not A alone.

Pinned by rotary_feed_cap: an_inch_program_posts_the_capped_feed_in_inch,
